'''Paul Michael Sutcliffe'''<ref name="sutcliffe1">{{cite journal |title=BSc |journal=University of Durham Congregation (28 June 9:10am) |date=1989 |page=6 |publisher=Durham University |location=Durham}}</ref> is British [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] and mathematician, currently Professor of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Durham]].<ref>[https://www.dur.ac.uk/research/directory/staff/?id=4476 Staff profile], University of Durham, retrieved 28 February 2016.</ref> He specialises in the study of [[topological soliton]]s.

He serves as the Project Director of the SPOCK (''Scientific Properties of Complex Knots'') research programme dedicated to the study of [[Knot (mathematics)|knotted]] structures.<ref>[http://www.maths.dur.ac.uk/spock/index.html/newpeople.html Meet the Research Programme Team] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513041407/http://www.maths.dur.ac.uk/spock/index.html/newpeople.html |date=13 May 2018 }}, retrieved 28 February 2016.</ref>   Related subjects of research include [[skyrmion]]s.

Sutcliffe was awarded the [[London Mathematical Society|LMS]] [[Whitehead Prize]] in 2006 for contributions to the study of [[topological soliton]]s and their dynamics.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200609/people.pdf Mathematics People, AMS Notices, September 2006]</ref>

==Education==
Sutcliffe graduated from [[Durham University]] in 1989.<ref name=sutcliffe1 />
